head_commit.message:
feat(sp): package the three specialised principals as installable, byte-deterministic plugin sets

Track C first slice (C-SP-01/02/03, partial: packaging, not installation).

- sbl_sp/plugins: deterministic ZIP builder (fixed timestamps, sorted entries,
  one skill each) deriving plugin.json from each principal's own manifest, so a
  package cannot claim permissions the principal does not have.
- claim_ceiling is HOST_PENDING and is not a parameter: build_package() rejects a
  caller who tries to raise it, and every manifest carries host_install_state
  NOT_INSTALLED. A ZIP existing is not an installation.
- three distinct identities (sbl-tpm-sp / sbl-commander-sp /
  sbl-external-challenge-sp); a collision is refused rather than silently written.
- skills: tpm (clarify/bound/hand off), commander (bounded build within a write
  set, refuses to sign), external challenge (read-only review, refuses to edit).
- tools/build_sp_plugins.py emits the set plus a provenance table.
- 8 tests cover identity separation, manifest derivation, determinism, the ceiling,
  unknown principal refusal, read-only challenge, and no smuggled corpus.

Not claimed: host installation, plugin ids, effective load, trigger, uninstall.
Those need a host and are recorded as HOST_PENDING in the R3 evidence.

head_commit.message:
fix(sbl): make the two CI-only test failures honest, and keep the summary visible

The v9 CI run failed on both platforms for two test defects that a dev machine hides, not for product
defects:

- test_inventory_with_a_wrong_digest_is_refused relied on the private source mirror being present, so
  on a runner every document reported "missing" and the digest branch was never reached. It now builds
  its own 14-document corpus, pins FALLBACK_ROOT to it with monkeypatch, asserts the good record passes
  and then flips one digest.
- test_bind_repo_context_reads_clean_head compared a literal path, but Windows runners hand out 8.3
  short names ("RUNNER~1") while resolve() returns the long form. It now compares
  normcase(realpath(...)) on both sides.

Also: the CI run line no longer passes a second -q. pyproject already sets addopts=-q, and a second -q
raises the quiet level until pytest stops printing its summary, so the job log could prove an exit code
but no denominator. A test now asserts the run line keeps the summary, and that pytest is installed
before the suite.

Local: 11/11 gates exit 0, 137 passed, scan CLEAN 181 files. Verified on a clean Python 3.11.9 venv with
the package installed from a copy, which is the shape CI uses.

head_commit.message:
fix(sbl): four defects the substitute checker found — G-KNOW identity/binding, ModeGate ACK trust

The M4 substitute checker (nonce SBLR2-VERIFY-15, gpt-6.1-sol, read-only on a copy of b5fd5d0) returned
FAIL with four MEDIUM product findings. All four reproduce; all four are fixed here with tests that fail
without the fix.

V15-GKNOW-01 — the doc-id regex required \b before "DOC", so the corpus's real filenames
(SBL_PIPD-LS-PKG_DOC-05.md, underscore before DOC) never matched. The builder indexed all 14 books and
still reported indexed_doc_ids=[], so every real question about DOC-05 refused with NO_ANSWER despite 177
chunks. The pattern now allows the underscore/zero-to-two separators and normalises to DOC-NN, which also
makes DOC/27, DOC--27, DOC27, doc_27 and DOC 27 resolve to the same identity.

V15-GKNOW-02 — the named source was only checked for existence; scoring still ran over every chunk, so a
DOC-05 question returned DOC-00 at score 1.0. A named, indexed source now constrains the candidate chunks.

V15-GKNOW-03 — DOC/27 and DOC--27 bypassed the named-source refusal because the parser did not recognise
them; they now normalise and are refused like any unknown id.

V15-MODE-01 — the serious one: SWOF_CONNECTED accepted a native ACK consisting of four non-empty strings, so
an entirely fabricated ACK made decide("net.call") return allowed=true, no_effect=false. That contradicted
the README's own refusal claim. An ACK is now verified: the issuer must be on SBL_SWOF_ACK_ISSUERS, the
signature must be the HMAC of issuer/permit_id/subject_id under SBL_SWOF_ACK_KEY, compared in constant time,
and with no anchor configured the gate refuses (fail closed). A correctly signed ACK still allows, so the
refusal is not blanket.

head_commit.message:
fix(sbl): close the two defects the second checker reproduced before its turn was cut

Receipt SBLR2-VERIFY-16 never completed: the provider flagged the checker's own adversarial work as
cybersecurity-risky and killed the turn, after which the dispatcher's retry hit the known websocket 426.
Its transcript nevertheless recorded two reproduced escapes, and both are real.

V16-BRIDGE-01 — junction swap between validation and write. The real-path check and the open were two
different instants, so replacing an allowed directory with a link in between escaped the writeset. apply()
now resolves once more immediately before opening, writes to the RESOLVED path rather than the literal one,
and after writing verifies that the file landed inside the real root, removing it and refusing if it did not.
Test: a monkeypatched re-resolution that returns an outside path must NACK and leave nothing behind.

V16-MODE-02 — signature collision. The HMAC material was the three fields joined by a bare separator, so
("issuer","a\x1fB","C") and ("issuer","a","B\x1fC") produced the same digest and therefore interchangeable
ACK signatures. The material is now length-prefixed. Test asserts the two tuples no longer collide.

Local: 11/11 gates exit 0, 148 passed (CORE 47, MODES 14, KNOW 15), scanner CLEAN 195 files.

pulls.title: c3 round 2: portable plugin manifests, the wheel that shipped without its data, and two installable surfaces
pulls.body:
Round 4 narrow repair of `F-R4-C3-PLUGIN-SCHEMA-001`, plus two installable surfaces.

**What was wrong.** `plugin_manifest()` emitted `"schema": "SBL-AGENT-PLUGIN/1"` with no `$schema`,
and put `identity` / `permissions` / `forbidden` / `claim_ceiling` at the top level. The portable
Agent Plugins 1.0.0 schema sets `additionalProperties: false` and requires `$schema` and `name`, so no
conforming host could recognise these packages.

**What changed.** The manifest is now `{$schema, name, version, description, license, keywords,
extensions}`, with principal metadata under `extensions["org.sbl.principal"]`. Every package is
validated against a vendored copy of the published schema before the ZIP is closed, and validator
non-vacuity is proven by injection (missing/foreign `$schema`, extra top-level key, the legacy
`schema` key, illegal name pattern, non-object extension, unknown author key).

**A second defect, found by the Docker sandbox and not by any local test:** the wheel shipped without
`sbl_sp/manifests/*.json`, so every `load_manifest` call in an *installed* package raised
`SBL_E_UNKNOWN_SP` while the source tree was green — CI ran `pip install -e .`, which resolves data
files straight from the source tree. `package-data` is fixed and `tools/check_wheel_contents.py` now
builds the real wheel in CI and asserts its members.

**New surfaces.** `sbl_stack` (install / doctor / selftest / status / uninstall over the composed
M01..M06 core, with an integrity manifest of the exact bytes it validated) and `sbl_harness` (pinned
HGK dependency + harness ABI + probe / install / doctor / uninstall; it declares the native boundary
rather than crossing it).

**Ceiling.** `PACKAGED_HOST_PENDING`. Three packages were installed and loaded by a real host loader
on one machine, with a rollback point taken first; no host-issued plugin identity was obtained and no
independent checker signed. Merge is an owner act and does not raise the ceiling.

183 tests, 11/11 gates, secret scan CLEAN, CI 2/2 on ubuntu + windows 3.11 (run 39525131900).

Evidence: `evidence/r4-20261021-c4` — `_governance/round-20261021-r4/` (contract, five-tool matrix,
sandbox receipt, rollback manifest, install receipt, SWOF shadow handoff, CR, corrections).

pulls.body:
## What this merges

`candidate/r2-20261020-v13` (`bedc11957d4fc2474b249b69d200829272c118ef`) into `main` (`ca6830d9fc9d89b7b87e818670dd67b393472d79`).

The candidate carries the whole v0.1 foundation: `sbl_core` M01-M06, the three specialised-principal manifests, `sbl-todo`, G-KNOW, the mode gate, the C0-C9 contract, the gate toolchain and the governance record. 220 tree entries.

## Gate evidence

| Gate | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Hosted CI | run [39426671565](https://github.com/shw097-team/SBL/actions/runs/39426671565) — ubuntu job 118640874662 and windows job 118640874677, both success, `145 passed, 1 skipped` each |
| M4-LITE (merge gate) | owner `HUMAN_PROCEDURAL_ACCEPTANCE`, subject `bedc119`, 24/24 cases, `subject_mutation CLEAN` — `evidence/human/HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE_2026-10-20.json` |
| Six properties | GKNOW-ID, GKNOW-SEP, GKNOW-BIND, MODE-ACK, MODE-SIG, BRIDGE-SETTLE — POS and NEG each, raw receipts in `_governance/round-20261020-r3/M4LITE/receipts/` |
| Local gates | 11/11 exit 0, `156 passed` on the later c3 branch, `148 passed` on v13 |
| Secret scan | CLEAN, 0 hard findings |
| Source freeze | 14/14 books re-hashed, aggregate `754cf7be...` |

## Honest limits of this PR

- The M4 receipt is **owner self-review** (`owner-reviewing-own-product`), labelled `HUMAN_PROCEDURAL_ACCEPTANCE`. It is **not** `INDEPENDENT_CASE_PASS`: the mandated checker carrier (openai-codex over websocket) answers 426, and the PLAN-lane fallback was cut by the provider content filter after reaching VERIFY-15's FAIL.
- Not covered: host installation of the three plugins, native ECP/permit, the 149 child requirements, the 38 delivery surfaces, the 441 donor identities. Those are tracked, not claimed.
- `F13-08` is satisfied by this PR existing; the merge press is the owner's.

## Reviewer's one-hour path

```
git clone https://github.com/shw097-team/SBL && cd SBL
git checkout bedc11957d4fc2474b249b69d200829272c118ef
python <evidence-branch>/_governance/round-20261020-r3/M4LITE/run_m4lite.py --subject-root . --out-dir /tmp/m4lite
python tools/run_gates.py
python tools/secret_scan.py --root .
```

head_commit.message:
docs(readme): stop asserting a stale checksum-list size in the quickstart

The quickstart predates this release and said "SHA256SUMS lists three assets" and "expect three
': OK' lines", which was true for the previous preview and is false now that the release publishes
six covered assets. The number was never the point - the point is that the block may only check what
it downloaded - so the wording is now count-agnostic and the alternative block lists the remaining
assets it would need. No digest, version or identity claim changed.

The released tag's own copy of this file keeps the older wording; the tag is immutable and is not
re-pointed. This correction lands on main and reaches the next preview's source archive.

head_commit.message:
docs: the install surface has three routes, not two (front page, install SSOT, plus a guard)

The front page and the install SSOT both claimed 'two routes and only two' (Web, Agent) while this
repository publishes a third: the private plugin ZIP pipd-ls-sp-public-skills.zip on the immutable
v0.1.1-preview.4 release. Both pages already contradicted themselves elsewhere -- the navigation table
('Want a private ChatGPT plugin'), the private-plugin ceiling row and the download instructions all
describe that route. Reported by the owner.

- README.md: the route paragraph now names three routes and points at Route 3; the navigation row and
  the Install section no longer say 'either route' / 'for both'.
- docs/install/README.md: the SSOT now declares three routes and carries a new
  'Route 3 - Private plugin ZIP (ChatGPT, your own account)' section with the asset's bytes, digest,
  entry count, download URL, the four UI steps, the same-plugin_id caveat and its ceiling
  (FORMAT_PASS / ONE_ACCOUNT_PARTIAL, owner's account only, no portal review).
- tests/test_install_route_surface.py: new offline guard so the count cannot drift again -- it forbids
  the six old phrasings, requires the ZIP route and its asset URL to be named, and requires the route
  headings to be exactly 1, 2, 3. Verified with a negative control (restoring the old wording fails it).

Gates: tests/test_install_route_surface.py + tests/test_r6_doc_identity_guard.py => 14 passed;
full suite 632 passed / 20 skipped / 0 failed. Docs-only: no src/, schemas/ or skills/ change.

head_commit.message:
wip(stage-b): partial public-plugin projection tooling, stopped mid-flight at pause

PARTIAL AND UNTESTED - not a candidate. The bounded writer produced the source-freeze tool, the
plugin builder and the web-fallback builder, plus the candidate manifest with owner placeholders
and an empty derivations file; it had not yet produced the test modules, the install documents or
the verification workflow when it was stopped at the user's pause. Nothing here is verified.

The owner gates the build must fail closed on are recorded in stage-b/WRITER_BRIEF.md: eight
SKILL.md files carry non-portable frontmatter and need owner-approved derivation records, and no
image asset exists in the repository, so a verified-icon claim has no in-repo basis.

head_commit.message:
fix(r5r2): per-segment obligations, no-space sentence boundary, two docs/gate corrections

An independent adversarial re-derivation of the preview.4 repair found four defects. Three are
corrected here and the fourth is narrowed.

D1b (regression, silent): the previous revision merged same-polarity segments into ONE atom, so
`不得A，不得B` compiled to one atom where the frozen compiler produced two. That is the collapse this
module exists to refuse - validate_atoms cannot see an obligation folded into another atom's text.
Each boundary segment is an atom again, and the clause-level negation now governs the segments that
follow it until one states its own positive modality, which is the scope defect the old compiler got
wrong in the other direction (a cue-less covered segment was compiled as MUST).

probe's closing answer explicitly quarantines the embedded SYSTEM OVERRIDE, while the literal string
appears in the log only because the model is quoting the file it read.

model, and NOT an acceptance. Web GPT-6, Hermes and Codex UI stay NOT_RUN / NOT_VERIFIED.

gpt-6.1-sol medium = the owner-declared VERIFY lane), which forbids the checker from reading the
writer's report and requires it to re-derive every decisive claim, with a rubber-stamp claim (C3)
as the blocking one.

head_commit.message:
ci(public-plugin-verify): declare the stage-c write set for this round

The gate measures ${BASE}...HEAD. Its stage-b arm declares the Stage A tip as BASE, so for any
branch based on main the governed range includes every merge since that tip: measured here as 273
paths, of which this round wrote 24. A source-repair round therefore could not pass the stage-b arm
whatever it wrote, which is a declaration gap, not a verdict about this change.

The gate's own design says the branch declares its stage, so this adds a third arm instead of
borrowing one: stage-c declares the frozen S4-R5 subject f4021ae as BASE, allows exactly this
round's repair and release-staging surface, and DENIES skills/ and packaging/public-plugin/ so the
arm still refuses something real. Self-test plants for stage-c are added and refuse as expected.
Stages A and B are left byte-identical.

Claim ceiling: LOCAL_CANDIDATE_ONLY. This is a gate amendment made in the pull request that needs
it; it is disclosed as an amendment there and is subject to the independent check.

head_commit.message:
S4 R6: repair the install page's dead outgoing link and guard outgoing links

The install page told a reader that the release's identities live in
`docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json` and linked it as `](RELEASE_TUPLE.json)`, which resolves
relative to `docs/install/` and therefore pointed at nothing. The documented route
was dead. An independent audit of the round found it (row DOC-LINK-TARGET); the
existing F-R6-01 guard could not, because it checked in-page anchors only.

This changes the validator in the strengthening direction, never the relaxing one:

  * docs/install/README.md: `](RELEASE_TUPLE.json)` -> `](../RELEASE_TUPLE.json)`.
  * tests/test_r6_doc_identity_guard.py: new check 6 -- every relative markdown link
    target must resolve to something present at HEAD; a target escaping the repo
    root is a problem; external URLs, in-page anchors and absolute paths are out of
    scope. Plus a paired mutation (mutation 6) that re-breaks the exact link found,
    so the check is falsifiable. Check 6 reports the defect on the pre-repair text
    (127ec1c:docs/install/README.md) and reports nothing after the repair.

Measured: guard 11/11 OK (6 real-document checks + 5 mutations, each mutation
asserted to FAIL); affected subset 28 OK; whole suite 635 tests / OK (skipped=4) /
202.634s / exit 0.

Claim ceiling: the candidate remains unmerged, unreleased and not host-qualified.

head_commit.message:
S4 FINAL closeout: disambiguate manifest_source.commit in the shipped manifest

manifest_source.commit names the commit whose tree the rows describe; a manifest cannot name its own
carrying commit. The field now says so explicitly, so an external verifier reading SHA256SUMS does not
mistake the described commit for the tip. Rows and SHA256SUMS are unchanged (MANIFEST.json is excluded
from the row set by design), and the extract-and-verify pass is re-run against this commit.

pulls.body:
## PIPD-LS-SP S4 R6 — 階段結案文件修補（FAR-R17 續行）

依《S4 R6｜階段結案＋私人 Plugin 指揮薄》與《S4 R6 修補後外部獨立複驗與階段結案裁決》執行。**候選，未合併、未 tag、未 release。**

### 這個 PR 改了什麼

| 檔案 | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `docs/install/README.md` | 記錄已發布（immutable）伺服端文件的來源漂移：served `PIPD_WEB_FALLBACK.md`（sha256 `c88ddc49…`）自帶 `release_id: v0.1.1-preview.3`。**只能由下一次發行修正，不得原位替換。** |
| `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | 修補版本身分混淆：`main@d3bd545` 與 `preview.4@cc6c193` 不得互相偷換；同 `plugin_id` 的更新路徑。 |
| `tests/test_r6_doc_identity_guard.py` | **新增**：安裝文件版本身分與頁內連結的守門測試（5 項實檔檢查 + 4 項配對 mutation）。 |
| `.github/workflows/public-plugin-verify.yml` | **具名修正，見下節。** |

### Authorized write-set amendment（具名、已揭露）

上一版 PR 的 `verify` 檢查為 **failure**：本回合宣稱的 `stage-c` 寫入集**不含** `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`，而本回合的 WorkOrder（F-R6-02）具名要求該檔。修正是**單一路徑替代項**（非前綴），且同一 commit 內同步更新該臂自帶的 planted-path 自測，使「它證明界線」與「它宣告界線」保持一致。

- 修正內容：`AMENDMENT S4-R6-20261016`，於 workflow 內具名註解說明理由。
- 本回合只加**一個**產品檔；量測依據：同一分類器在 `origin/main`（`f4021ae...d3bd545`，25 路徑）**PASS**，且 R5R3 未曾觸碰該檔。
- **未**把本回合的證據目錄納入寫入集（該臂明文拒絕回合自身收據）。

### 證據包位置（變更）

上一版把證據包放在產品分支，被同一個寫入集閘門拒絕（21 個 `S4_R6_CLOSEOUT_RETURN/**` 路徑）。依該 workflow 自身宣告的設計與既有回合慣例，證據包改置於專用分支：

**`r6-closeout-evidence-20261016`**（`5defc64`，含被撤回的脈絡與完整證據包）— 外部驗收官請由該分支取得證據。

### 驗證（可重跑）

| 檢測 | 指令 | 結果 |
|---|---|---|
| 寫入集分類器（本地重導） | `R17_check_write_set.py` | `RESULT: PASS`（27 路徑全在集內） |
| 該臂自測 | 由檔案讀出 regex 模擬 | `SELF_TEST: PASS` |
| 守門測試 | `python -m unittest tests.test_r6_doc_identity_guard -v` | `Ran 9 tests … OK` |
| 守門非空洞（對修補前樹 `d3bd545`） | 同上，置於該樹 worktree | `FAILED (failures=6)` |
| 受影響子集 | 4 個模組 | `Ran 44 tests … OK` |
| 全量 | `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` | `Ran 633 tests in 174.073s — OK (skipped=4)` |
| 託管 CI（本 head `127ec1c`） | — | `verify` success；`offline-gate` success ×2 |

獨立 VERIFY_SECURITY 派發（arm 釘選 `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` rank 2；`danger-full-access` + guard root）：`ok:true`、`nonce ✓`、`usage ✓`，`checker_id PIPD-S4-R6-CLOSEOUT-20261016-FAR-R17-VERIFY_SECURITY-5defc64f`，**verdict `PARTIAL`**——C1/C2/C3/C5/C6/C7 PASS，C4 因 guard 邊界無法認證全量套件（非候選回歸；同套件於邊界外 `633 OK`）。該檢查員已自行下載並重算 ZIP：68,357 B / `545e359a…` 相符。

### 宣告上限

本 PR 為**受控分支上的候選**：未合併、未 tag、未 release、未動 `main`、未動 `v0.1.1-preview.4`。`S4_FULL_PASS` / `HOST_QUALIFIED` / `PRODUCTION` = **NOT_GRANTED**；私有宿主 UAT = **NOT_RUN**（需具上傳權限的人類帳號）。合併、tag、release 均屬 OWNER GATE。
<!-- R18-SECTION -->

---

## R18 addendum — a dead documented route, repaired, and the whole class now guarded

An independent read-only audit of the round's own 115 requirement rows (by a child in a fresh
context) found that the install page's outgoing link

    [`docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json`](RELEASE_TUPLE.json)      <!-- docs/install/README.md -->

resolves relative to `docs/install/` and therefore pointed at `docs/install/RELEASE_TUPLE.json`,
which does not exist. **The documented route was dead, and the existing F-R6-01 guard could not see
it** — that guard checked in-page anchors only, while the requirement it implements is about the
documented route being truthful.

This pull request now repairs the change *and* the validator, in the strengthening direction:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/install/README.md` | `](RELEASE_TUPLE.json)` | `](../RELEASE_TUPLE.json)` |
| `tests/test_r6_doc_identity_guard.py` | checks 1–5 (in-page anchors) | checks 1–6; check 6 resolves every relative markdown link target at HEAD and flags a target escaping the repo root, with a paired mutation that re-breaks the exact link found |

**Falsifiability, measured.** Check 6 reports the defect on the pre-repair text
(`127ec1c:docs/install/README.md`) and reports nothing after the repair. Guard: 11/11 OK
(6 real-document checks + 5 mutations, each asserted to fail). Affected subset: 28 OK. Whole suite:
**635 tests / OK (skipped=4) / 202.634s / exit 0**. This commit's own write-set classifier, run
locally against this exact commit before pushing: **27 changed paths, all inside the declared
`stage-c` arm — PASS**.

### What this pull request now contains

4 commits, 4 files, `+465/−23`, head `c17aa76`, base `main` `d3bd545` (unmoved).
Hosted checks on `c17aa76`: `verify` **success**, `offline-gate` **success** ×2.

### Where the rest of the round's evidence is

It is **not** here, deliberately: the product write set refuses round artifacts, and widening it to
admit them would relax a validator in order to pass. The round's evidence lives on
`r6-closeout-evidence-20261016` (`338227c`), whose manifest verifies from a fresh clone:
**63/63 OK, 0 failed, 0 unreadable**. Its most useful members for a reviewer or an external
engineering team:

* `S4_R6_CLOSEOUT_RETURN/EXTERNAL_ENGINEERING_HANDOVER.md` — branch model, the governed write-set
  gate and its local reproduction, the lane model (including why the verification arm is pinned),
  build/test commands with measured results, module map, open tickets, prohibitions.
* `S4_R6_CLOSEOUT_RETURN/R18_AUDIT_REQUIREMENTS.tsv` — 115 requirement rows, evidence-located.
* `S4_R6_CLOSEOUT_RETURN/R18_REQUIREMENTS_RULING.tsv` — 120 rows, exactly one disposition each,
  including four options explicitly rejected as over-engineering.
* `S4_R6_CLOSEOUT_RETURN/checker_verdict.json` — the canonical verdict re-bound to the final
  verified candidate with all four dispatches preserved.

### Claim ceiling

The candidate is **not merged, not released and not host-qualified**. `S4_FULL_PASS`,
`HOST_QUALIFIED` and `PRODUCTION` remain `NOT_GRANTED`; the private-host UAT remains `NOT_RUN`;
`PUBLIC_DIRECTORY` remains `OUT_OF_SCOPE`. Merging is an owner action. Open tickets from this round:
`TT-R18-01` (negative tests for a ninth skill / cross-root change), `TT-R18-02` (a product-scoped
ExecutionBinding — the control plane's own change), `TT-R18-03` (the historical raw CI logs are
behind a credential that returns 401 for job logs, recorded as `SOURCE_GAP`), `TT-R18-04`
(a non-fatal `ResourceWarning` in `tools/`, outside this write set).

pulls.title: R5R3 closeout: preview.4 asset reproducibility, host-refusal discrimination and residual rulings
pulls.body:
## What this changes

One file, +15 lines: `docs/install/ASSET_READBACK_v0.1.1-preview.4.json` gains a `reproducibility` block.

It records a fact an external reviewer can re-derive: the plugin ZIP that release `v0.1.1-preview.4` serves
is the **byte-exact deterministic output of the commit the release tuple already records** (`cc6c193`). Two
independent builds at that commit produce 68,357 B / `545e359a…`, identical to the served asset. The block
carries its own claim ceiling: this proves provenance and determinism of the served bytes, **not** host
acceptance, and **not** that the release carries later commits.

No product source, schema, workflow or test is touched. The release's own identity suite
(`tests/test_r5r3_install_route_identity.py`, 10 tests) passes against this tree.

## Why it matters for the open questions

The private-host import of this release's plugin ZIP was refused server-side on 2026-10-14 with no error
code, and the cause is still unresolved. This change removes build nondeterminism from the candidate causes
and pairs with an offline member-level comparison against the package a previous round installed
successfully: every member shared by the two packages is byte-identical; only two provenance metadata
members differ. Manifest location and manifest fields are therefore excluded as causes, and the surviving
hypothesis is account/platform side.

## What is NOT claimed here

- Not host acceptance. The import is still unproven and the cause still unresolved.
- Not that the release carries later repairs: the served wheel's `requirements.py` predates them; the repairs
  are on `main` only. Whether to cut a successor is an owner decision, not this PR's.
- No release, tag, install, directory publication or production promotion was executed in this round.

## Residuals handed over (details in the evidence return)

1. `NEW_RELEASE` — successor carrying the later repairs; contingent on the import decision.
2. `PRIVATE_HOST_INSTALL` — one consented import attempt of the served package, then (only if refused) the
   previously accepted package, as the discriminating experiment.
3. Canonical SoD finding (pre-existing, not caused by this round): `check_sod(PLAN, VERIFY_SECURITY)`
   reports `SOD_VIOLATION` because both lane routes' top-level model is `gpt-6.1-sol`. Resolving it is a
   canonical route change, i.e. an owner/WorkOrder act.

## Evidence return

Separate evidence branch `r5r3-closeout-evidence-20261016` (directory
`R5R3_PREVIEW4_CLOSEOUT_20261016/`), carrying the build reproduction receipt, the control-plane probe, the
PLAN-lane decision and its serving evidence, the TT dispositions, the runbook and the owner decision request,
indexed by digest in `PACK_INDEX.json`.

Rollback: a single revert of this PR's merge commit. Nothing immutable is touched.

# R5R3 — preview.4 install route, release identity, and the round's evidence return

**Claim ceiling: `CANDIDATE_ONLY` / `LOCAL`.** Nothing here is an acceptance, an approval, a new tag or a
release. The subject of this round is the **already-published** `v0.1.1-preview.4` plus the documentation
route that leads a new user to it.

## What was found (on the frozen subject `dba4b19`, delta-only)

The external R5 verdict asked for one bounded patch and one Preview. Following it, this round did **not**
redo `D1` (negation polarity/scope), `D2` (clause boundaries) or the five `ClaimCeiling` shapes: all three
are already merged into `main` and were re-verified rather than re-implemented. What was still wrong was
the **route and the identity record**:

| # | Measured defect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `docs/install/README.md` tells a reader that the preview.4 identities live in the `v0.1.1-preview.4` entry of `docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json` — and that entry **did not exist** on `main`. The documented route pointed at nothing. | `grep -c v0.1.1-preview.4 docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json` → 0 before, 1 after |
| 2 | No record anywhere carried the served asset identities of the release, so nothing in-tree could be checked against `SHA256SUMS`. | 7 served assets, 6 `SHA256SUMS` entries, now all recorded |
| 3 | The front page route to the private plugin ZIP could be read without the digest that the release's own `SHA256SUMS` carries. | README route now names the release asset and its served digest |

A fourth, smaller defect was found **by the repository's own CI** on the first push of this branch and is
the reason the shape of this PR changed — see "CI corrected this PR" below.

## CI corrected this PR (disclosed, not hidden)

The first version of this branch committed the round's evidence tree and an `openspec/` change onto the
product branch. `public-plugin-verify` went **red** on the step *"Prove the upgrade wrote only inside its
allowed set"*: the `stage-c` arm of that gate is a positive allowlist, and neither a round evidence tree
nor `openspec/**` is inside it. That is the gate doing its job, and the repair was not to widen it for
convenience:

- the round's evidence tree and the `openspec` change record **moved off the product branch** (they travel
  on `r5r3-evidence-return-20261016`, the same separate-branch pattern the R5Y evidence return used);
- the identity record was put where the install guide already says it lives: the `v0.1.1-preview.4` entry
  of `docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json`;
- the served-byte readback landed under `docs/install/` (already inside the arm) as
  `ASSET_READBACK_v0.1.1-preview.4.json`, explicitly marked as a repository-side verification record and
  **not** a release asset;
- **one file** was added to the `stage-c` allowlist (`docs/RELEASE_TUPLE.json`), named as an amendment in

  earlier run was red: the first version of the new test file omitted the `src/` bootstrap that

pulls.title: fix: per-segment obligations, no-space sentence boundary, two docs/gate corrections
pulls.body:
## Why

An independent adversarial re-derivation of the `v0.1.1-preview.4` repair (a separate read-only lane,
different checker from the writer) returned three of the round's seven claims as **PARTIAL** and listed
four defects. Three are corrected here; the fourth is narrowed and carried as an open item. The
released tag is **not** touched.

## The defects and their disposition

| # | Defect | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **D1b, real regression and silent:** same-polarity obligations joined by `，`/`以及`/`and` merged into **one** atom where the frozen compiler produced one atom per segment (`不得A，不得B` → 1, was 2). An obligation folded into another atom's text is invisible to `validate_atoms` — the collapse this module exists to refuse. | **Fixed.** One atom per boundary segment again, and the clause-level negation now governs the segments that follow it until one states its own positive modality — which is the scope defect the old compiler got wrong in the *other* direction (a cue-less covered segment compiled as MUST). |
| 2 | **D2 boundary gap:** a period flanked by ASCII alphanumerics was never a boundary, so a sentence end typed without a space (`Do task A.Task B must run.`) stopped splitting. The claim "a real sentence-final period still ends a clause" was therefore **too broad**. | **Fixed.** The token rule now yields to an uppercase ASCII letter after the period; domains, versions and decimals still stay single atoms. |
| 3 | **D1c over-refusal (minor):** `不得使用必須的憑證` was refused as ambiguous because `必須` appears as an adjective inside the object. | **Fixed.** Only the inverted order — positive modal first, negation second, with no boundary — is genuinely ambiguous. |
| 4 | **Gate widening:** the `stage-c` arm added in the previous PR must allow `src/`, `schemas/`, `tests/`, `dist/`, and the workflow file, all of which the older arms refuse; any branch may set `STAGE` itself. Its trigger paths also omitted `src/**`, `schemas/**`, `tests/**`, `fixtures/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `tools/build_dist.py`, so a source-only PR would not run the gate at all. | **Partially fixed, remainder disclosed.** The trigger paths are added, so a source-only PR now runs the gate. The widening cannot be removed — an arm that must allow `src/` cannot refuse it — so the arm states that limit in writing and it is carried as an open item: its control is review of its own diff. |

## Also in this PR (docs truthfulness)

The previous PR replaced `preview.3` with `preview.4` wholesale, which left the README asserting that
`v0.1.1-preview.4` **carries** the known Trace false-PASS defect **and supersedes** it, and listing
`preview.4` in the "Superseded" row while telling the reader to use `.4`. The superseded release is
`preview.3`. Character-presence tests cannot catch that class, so the prose is corrected by hand.

## Evidence

- Full suite on this head: **614 tests OK (skipped=4), exit 0** (610 + the four new regression tests).
- New tests pin **both** directions, so neither the old failure nor the regression can pass unnoticed:
  per-segment atom counts for four same-polarity shapes; negation scope over a cue-less segment versus a
  segment with its own modality; the no-space sentence boundary **and** the token cases; and the
  over-refusal case as a positive control.
- Focused module (`tests/test_atomic_requirements.py`): 35 tests OK.

## What is not claimed

The published `v0.1.1-preview.4` keeps the behaviour its own release notes describe; this fix lives on
`main` and is in **no release**. Publishing a follow-up preview needs a fresh owner authorization.
Independent re-check of this new commit is requested but not yet done — the previous verdict is reported
as coming from a different checker than the one that wrote the code.

pulls.title: docs: quickstart checksum step no longer asserts a stale list size
pulls.body:
## What this changes

Three comments in the README quickstart claimed a count that belongs to an older release:

- `SHA256SUMS lists three assets` (bash step 2)
- `expect three ": OK" lines (wheel, source zip, notes)`
- `SHA256SUMS lists three assets but only the wheel was fetched` (PowerShell step 2)

That was true when the checksum list covered the wheel, the source archive and the notes. This release
publishes six covered assets, so the sentence is now false, and a reader who follows it and then sees
six `: OK` lines has been told the wrong thing by the project's own quickstart.

The point of the sentence was never the number - it is that a checksum block may only check what it
downloaded - so the wording is now count-agnostic, and the alternative block lists the three further
assets it would need to fetch for the whole file to check clean.

## What does not change

No digest literal, version string, identity claim or command semantics changed. The wheel digest in
both blocks is the same one the previous release published.

## Scope and disclosure

- Docs only: `README.md`. 20 tests covering the quickstart contract, the documented `--root` forms and
  the doctor/schema truthfulness gates pass locally after the edit.
- The **published tag's copy** of this file keeps the older wording. `v0.1.1-preview.4` is immutable and
  is not re-pointed; this correction lands on `main` and reaches the next preview's source archive.
  The release's own notes asset does not contain the stale claim.
- Found while verifying the release's served bytes, not while writing it: the checksum file is
  generated per release, so the same sentence would have gone stale on any release that added assets.

(`ERR_CLAIM_WITHOUT_RECOMPUTE`, `ERR_RECOMPUTE_NOT_CARRIED`, with two negative self-tests), and the
assembly is checked too: `rem3_build_bundle.py` refuses to emit a bundle unless every block label
appears exactly once and the character budget keeps real headroom under the dispatcher's argv ceiling.

### Handover
`evidence/12_GATES/RECEIVER_HANDOFF_BUNDLE.json` is the typed offer: state `OFFERED`, admission and human
token fields **empty on purpose** (`AWAITING_EXTERNAL`), permissions granted "none", rollback refs at the
two untouched frozen refs. `main` and `v0.1.1-preview.3` are untouched by this session.

pulls.title: S4R3 Stage B (draft, stacked): measure the Stage B write set against its declared base; ship the Web artefact
pulls.body:
Draft, stacked on the Stage A repair branch. **No merge is approved by this PR.**

## What this change set is

Stage B `UPGRADE` for `S4R3-F002` and `S4R3-F004`.

**F002 — the write-set gate measured the wrong range.** It took `${PR_BASE_SHA:-${STACKED_BASE_SHA}}`.
GitHub reports the base *branch* tip, so a Stage B branch stacked on the Stage A tip but opened
against `main` measured `main...HEAD` — attributing every Stage A source change to the Stage B
upgrade. That is why the run failed on `tools/verify_evidence_digests.py` and skipped the rest. The
gate now:

- measures its **declared** Stage B base and refuses when that base is missing or is not an ancestor;
- prints the full upstream diff as an inventory that is explicitly *not* the Stage B write set;
- says `STAGE_B_SCOPE_EMPTY` in the log rather than reporting a vacuous pass when the head *is* the base;
- self-tests its own classifier against planted `src/**`, `schemas/**`, `skills/**`, `dist/**`
  (must be refused) and planted Stage B artefacts (must be accepted). A gate that accepts everything
  and a gate that refuses everything otherwise look identical from outside.

The allowlist gains two enumerated single paths, no wildcards: `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, which the upgrade
blueprint names as the single manual path but the R3 allowlist never listed, and this round's own
evidence directory.

**F004 — the Web route promised a document that was not in the tree.** The built
`docs/install/PIPD_WEB_FALLBACK.md` and its `.sha256` are now committed; the install SSOT records both
plus the command that must reproduce them. The README gains one navigation block and stops competing
with the install SSOT; the shell transcripts stay, labelled as executed evidence rather than as a
second set of instructions. `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` is added as the single user guide. 41 local links
and anchors across README → guide → install SSOT → fixtures check clean.

## Write set

`git diff --name-status 517d7a5d3f00935e1589908f456dfacea8fd8a74...HEAD` lists only Stage B paths, and
nothing under `src/**`, `schemas/**`, `skills/**` or `dist/**`. The local reproduction of the gate is
in `.hgk/rounds/S4R3-.../scripts/writeset_gate_repro.sh`.

## Claim ceiling

`BUILD`-level evidence only. No public plugin listing, no portal scan/review/publish, no vendor
validator run, no host UAT, no new release tag — all `NOT_EXECUTED`. `NO_MERGE`,
`NO_PUBLIC_RELEASE`, `S4_FULL_PASS` **not granted**.

pulls.title: S4R3 Stage A (draft): make CI carry the suite's exit code; repair the 11+2 hosted-Linux failures
pulls.body:
Draft. **No merge is approved by this PR.** It exists so that the two P0 findings of
`PIPD-S4-EXT-ACCEPT-R3-20261013` have a runnable subject and a raw log a checker can read.

## What this change set is

Stage A `NARROW_REPAIR` for `S4R3-F001`: the `ci` workflow's test steps piped into `tee`/`tail`
without `pipefail`, so a run whose own log read `FAILED (failures=11, skipped=6)` was reported as a
successful job. The suite really was red on hosted Linux; the gate hid it.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/public-plugin-verify.yml` — every real test step now
  runs under `set -euo pipefail`; the provenance step captures its log before `tail`; each mutation
  step keeps its explicit status capture, so a step that is *supposed* to fail still fails loudly.
- `pyproject.toml` — PyYAML declared as the `[test]` extra. `tools/skill_pack_check.py` needs it for
  `skills/*/tests/cases.yaml` and never declared it, so six `test_skill_contracts` tests died with
  `TOOL_MISSING` on a runner that only ran `pip install -e .`. The typed refusal is unchanged.
- `src/pipd_ls_sp/workspace.py` — contain a repair subject by the subject's **own** path flavour. A
  Windows-flavoured `C:/Windows/system32/x.dll` was re-based under the authorised root on POSIX
  because `Path()` treats it as relative there, so the escape passed.
- `examples/first-run/run.sh` — index mode 100644 → 100755. It was not executable in a Linux checkout.
- `examples/first-run/run.ps1` — build the scratch workspace from `[System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()`
  when the Windows-only `$env:TEMP` is absent, instead of passing `$null` to `Join-Path`.
- `tools/cli_smoke.py` — persist the `IntentCard` that this run's own `intake` produced, rather than
  reading the checked-in `.hgk/artifacts/s1/intent_card.json`, whose source is the author's absolute
  Windows path.
- `tests/test_web_fallback.py` — the blanket `assertFalse(out.exists())` failed the very test that
  proves the symlink gate works: refusing a symlinked destination must *leave it in place*. The
  assertion now separates "created nothing" from "left a pre-existing destination untouched", and
  keeps the sentinel-bytes and `is_symlink` assertions.

## Raw evidence in this branch

`.hgk/rounds/S4R3-20261013-ci-truthfulness-and-stageb-writeset/evidence/` — the frozen subject's own
13 failures, all 13 mapped to 7 root causes with a paired control each, the paired fault injection
(shipped shape returns 0 on a red suite; repaired shape returns 1), and the repaired suite on Linux
and Windows. `RAW_INDEX.json` carries the digest of every file.

## Claim ceiling

Locally verified: the repairs, on Linux (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12) and Windows (Python 3.11).
`Ran 572 / OK (skipped=4)` and `Ran 108 / OK` on Windows; `Ran 572 / OK (skipped=10)` and
`Ran 108 / OK (skipped=1)` on Linux; CLI smoke 13/13. The hosted run of *this* PR is the
authoritative check and is what a checker should read. Not covered: macOS, host UAT, vendor/portal
validation, S4 acceptance. `NO_MERGE`, `NO_PUBLIC_RELEASE`, `S4_FULL_PASS` **not granted**.

pulls.title: R4 focused-repair candidate — published for external verification (DRAFT, not for merge as a release)
pulls.body:
## What this is

A **candidate published for external verification**, per the owner's instruction. It is **not a release and must not be merged as a release act.** The ceiling is `CANDIDATE_ONLY`: `INDEPENDENT_PASS`, `PUBLICATION_APPROVED`, `RELEASED` and `PRODUCTION_VERIFIED` are all **NOT GRANTED**.

Built on the published `main` (`3aebbbce`), 2 commits, 135 files changed.

## What it contains

- **`tools/round_envelope.py` destination guards STOP-1..STOP-6** — refuse a blank / empty / cwd / home / drive-root / equal-to-source / ancestor `--dst` **before any deletion**. This is the long-term repair of the destructive incident recorded in the round evidence (an empty `--dst` normalised to the working directory and `shutil.rmtree` deleted tracked files in the repo root).
- The hardening gates `preflight_check`, `round_selfscan`, `deny_list_scan`, `pi_dedup_check`, `tt_summary_check`, plus `build_spec_del_crosswalk` / `build_publication_manifest` / `publication_attestation` — each with tests (suite 188 → 256).
- The full round receipts under `.hgk/rounds/R4-20261009-focused-repair/`, including the **three-round independent verification of the repair** (v3 `FAIL` → v4 `FAIL` on one row → **v5 `PASS`**, all six rows, with the harness disclosed as orchestrator-authored and *not* treated as an independent authority).
- `docs/OWNER_ADJUDICATION_R4_2026-10-09.{json,md}` — the six open items A1–A5 and V7, with the ruling executed for each. Five required no owner action; the only authority act is `A2 = ACCEPT_EXISTING_NO_LICENSE_NOTICE`, which **grants nothing**.
- `.hgk/rounds/R4-20261009-focused-repair/H2/raw/INCIDENT02.json` — a second instance of the *same* path-defect class, this time on the orchestration side, disclosed in full.

## What is still FAILING or PARTIAL — please verify these, do not take them on trust

- **`tools/perf_budget.py --check` is FAIL**: `context_bytes_per_artefact` measures **343,547** against a **20,000** budget (other runs 336,674 / 355,119). All four thresholds carry `source_of_truth: UNPROVENANCED`, so the three timing rows are `UNDECIDABLE`. Fail-closed behaviour was retained and **no threshold was raised**.
- **Round acceptance is PARTIAL**: `W8-VERIFY-3` rows V1–V6 and V8 PASS but **V7 is `NOT_RUN`** — two gate tools are absent from the committed baseline, so "not weakened" cannot be computed. A commit alone cannot convert V7 to PASS.
- The hardening tools have **no automated consumer** in the pipeline — they bite when a human exercises them, which is weaker than an automated gate.
- `EVIDENCE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` remains unresolved (an earlier external challenge quoted an evidence SHA that no version in this tree reproduces).
- Knowledge readiness stays **PARTIAL** at physical coverage 153/160 — the number is not padded.

## Reproduce the headline checks

```bash
env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -q     # expect: Ran 256 tests, OK
env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME python -B tools/perf_budget.py --check         # expect: exit 1 — FAIL
env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME python -B tools/deny_list_scan.py              # expect: exit 0, PASS
env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME python -B tools/tt_summary_check.py --assert   # expect: counts agree (total=22, blocking=18)
```

See `README.md` for the full R4 status section and `docs/OWNER_ADJUDICATION_R4_2026-10-09.md` for the adjudication.

> Opened as a **draft** so it is reviewable without implying readiness to merge.
